title: introduce-cluster-slack-allocator-and-burst-throttle-gate
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally face bursty traffic that transiently exceeds committed capacity and existing burst credit pools. We need a cluster-level slack allocator that dynamically carves short-lived slack budgets from underutilized pools and a gating mechanism at the ingress to avoid amplification storms when reclaimed capacity is delayed. This PR implements a Cluster Slack Allocator (CSA) and a Burst Throttle Gate (BTG) to improve throughput guarantees and reduce end-to-end latency tail during multi-tenant bursts.

Summary of changes: - New runtime controller (cluster/slack_allocator.go) implementing CSA with time-weighted slack accounting and per-pool fairness heuristics. - Ingress gate component (gateway/burst_throttle_gate.go) that consults CSA via a lightweight API to accept/reject burst requests and emit backpressure signals compatible with the existing gateway circuit. - Telemetry: introduce slack_utilization and burst_gate_decisions metrics with percentile sampling and per-pool tagging (telemetry/metrics.go). - Autoscaler integration: the allocator exports short-lived allocation hints to the fleet autoscaler, enabling opportunistic warm-pool adjustments without violating reservation contracts. - Tests: unit tests for allocator invariants, integration test that replays synthetic burst traces to validate fairness and latency impact. - Docs: configuration docs and tuning guide (docs/dedicated/cluster-slack.md).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc link: internal/ENG-6421 (architecture and tradeoffs) - [x] Unit tests added for allocator invariants - [x] Integration harness replayed against perf-lab traces - [x] Backwards-compatible config defaults - [x] Canary plan included in release notes

Commits (high level): 1) initial prototype of CSA and gate (wip, refactor) 2) add metrics and telemetry labels 3) autoscaler hint integration and config knobs 4) add unit + integration tests 5) fix edge case for eviction while reallocating slack 6) performance tweaks (lock-free path for common case) 7) docs and release notes 8) address reviewers comments and CI fixes

Files changed (high level): - cluster/slack_allocator.go - gateway/burst_throttle_gate.go - autoscaler/hints.go - telemetry/metrics.go - docs/dedicated/cluster-slack.md - tests/allocator_invariants_test.go - tests/integration_burst_replay_test.go - internal/config/defaults.yaml - internal/config/schema_v2.go - build/ci/flake-retry.sh - go.mod - go.sum

Behavioral notes (what this does at runtime): - CSA periodically samples per-pool utilization and computes a short-duration slack budget (usually 30-120s) using an exponential decay window. - Slack budgets are fractionally loaned to requesting pools with proportional fairness and a configurable max-burst-per-pool cap. - The BTG intercepts incoming requests tagged as bursty; it queries CSA for available budget and returns either PASS, DELAY (short throttle token issued), or REJECT. DELAY responses carry a short TTL token that the gateway can queue with a bounded wait to smooth spikes. - When CSA reclaims slack (e.g., utilization rises), it emits a voluntary revoke signal; the BTG converts revoke events into early DELAY/REJECT decisions and logs diagnostic traces for tracing. - The autoscaler receives hints (not hard commits) to opportunistically warm GPUs; hints are advisory and respect reservation accounting by default.

Performance and safety: - Added fast-path in allocator that avoids locks for common accept flow; benchmarks show ~1.8x throughput for gate decision path compared to previous best-effort admission. - Fail-open semantics: if CSA becomes unavailable, BTG falls back to conservative static burst caps to preserve safety. - All config knobs default to conservative values to avoid changing behavior for existing fleets unless explicitly enabled.

Review discussion (condensed): Reviewer: Jun Park: "Allocator looks solid; concerns around race between reclaim and autoscaler hints—can we add a linearizable handoff?" Author: "Added a short-lived lease token and extended tests to simulate concurrent reclaim; lease avoids double-counting and is documented in config." Reviewer: Marcus Li: "Metrics look useful but could be high-cardinality. Limit per-pool labels to pool-id truncated to 8 chars." Author: "Truncated tags and added a sampled dimension for high-cardinality pools; updated telemetry/metrics.go." Reviewer: Olivia Chen: "We need a canary plan. Add incremental rollout steps and a rollback knob." Author: "Canary plan added to docs and release_notes field; added runtime flag 'csa.enable' for swift rollback."

CI summary: - Initial CI run failed (race detected in allocator unit tests under -race); I fixed the race by switching a condition to atomic and re-ran. - Integration perf job showed small memory spike which was mitigated by a pool object reuse change. - Final CI: all checks pass (unit, integration, lint, gosec).

Testing / validation: - Unit tests cover allocator invariants (no double-allocation, fairness under contention). - Integration replay runs on perf-lab dataset: 1M requests replayed across 120s bursts, showing 23% fewer 95th percentile latency spikes and 12% improved throughput under the same reserved capacity vs baseline. - Canary rollout plan: 5% of traffic in canary pool -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with metric thresholds and automatic rollback on tail-latency regressions.

Related work: Compared to reservoir-based designs, CSA focuses on short-duration slack loans with stronger fairness and ingress-level gating to avoid queue amplification. It complements existing warm-pool and credit-based systems rather than replacing them.

Release notes: - feature: cluster slack allocator and burst throttle gate to improve burst handling and reduce latency tail on dedicated fleets. - telemetry: new metrics slack_utilization and burst_gate_decisions. - config: csa.max_burst_per_pool, csa.window_seconds, csa.enable (default false).

Merge outcome: squash-and-merge after approvals. Changelog entry created and included in release candidate for dedicated platform v1.9.

Operational runbook (summary): - If observed "csa-unavailable" events, set csa.enable=false and watch gateway throttle rate; follow rollback instructions in docs/dedicated/cluster-slack.md. - To tune: adjust csa.window_seconds (shorter = more nimble, longer = more stable) and csa.max_burst_per_pool (cap per-tenant).

release_notes: Introduce cluster slack allocator (CSA) and a gateway burst throttle gate (BTG). Improves burst handling for dedicated fleets, adds telemetry metrics slack_utilization and burst_gate_decisions. Defaults disabled; enable via csa.enable=true and tune window_seconds and max_burst_per_pool.
